sections.title: 1. Credentials and the data red line
sections.summary: Highest priority, non-negotiable: credentials never enter the repository or any conversation artifact; the committed surface (game settings / playbook / experience-growth Mod / evolution output) is equally off limits for sensitive values, and every example uses synthetic data.
sections.source: Runtime projection of AGENTS.md data red line and docs/design/mod/tool-bridge.md (credential resolution); not an independent authority

rules.text: Never write a credential, key or token into the repository — including code, documentation, commit messages and Mod example data.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history)

rules.text: Never write a credential into any conversation artifact: reports, summaries, issue/PR descriptions, pasted log excerpts.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history)

rules.text: No sensitive information may enter a committed resource — the committed surface explicitly includes: game settings `data/config.json`, the playbook resources under `data/playbook/` (the head plus the chapter fragments assembled at load), the experience/growth (evolution) Mod and its output, and every other Mod resource or document committed with the repository.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-10-29 (s1 addition, not in the original AGENTS.md)

rules.text: The runtime KV family `settings.*` is no exception for sensitive values: the static defaults (`data/config.json`) and the dynamic overrides (`settings.*` written by `config.set`) only ever hold non-sensitive behavior switches, numbers and experience text (such as `evolution.mode` / `gates.require_all_green` / `evolution.max_per_run`).
rules.basis: the in-place 「设计依据」 sections of the governing contracts (ex-CONTEXT §5; user decision added 2026-10-29)

rules.text: Sensitive values — LLM API keys, tokens, database/object-storage connection strings, subagent model parameters (`YGG_SUBAGENT_*`) — live only in the local `.env` / `.env.local` (both git-ignored) and in no other file.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-10-29 (s1 addition); historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) + docs/context/rituals/dispatch.md §2

rules.text: Mod resources and reports may show key names only (such as `YGG_LLM_*`, `YGG_SUBAGENT_MODEL`), never values — including narrative text, `beats`/`prompts`, the closing review and any walk report.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-10-29 (s1 addition); historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) rule 2

rules.text: End-of-run evolution output (suggestion text, the review artifact, and any resource edit made from it) also counts as committed surface: never write a sensitive value into a Mod or a report as "accumulated experience".
rules.basis: user decision 2026-10-29 (s1 addition); `data/config.json` evolution.allow_paths

rules.text: Local development credentials always go through `.env` / `.env.local` (both git-ignored, mode 600); `.env.example` carries key names only, never values.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) rule 1

rules.text: Reports, documentation, commit messages and Mod example data show key names only, never values.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) rule 2

rules.text: Examples and test data are always synthetic; never introduce real personal data.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) rule 3

rules.text: After a violation, list honestly what was exposed (the specific file plus the content location), without downplaying or arguing; then stop the affected operations and wait for the user.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) rule 4

sections.title: 2. Repository shape
sections.summary: A Rust five-crate workspace plus pnpm packages, a Godot client and the in-repo .ygg harness; three shape invariants: a single source for decisions, a single source for schemas, and a zero-dependency core.

rules.text: The decision tables in the 「设计依据」 sections of the governing contracts are the single source of truth for project decisions; any new decision produced by a design discussion (Lua 唯一可执行接口+) must be written back into those tables.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (constraint 1)

rules.text: An implementation that conflicts with the decision table is a defect: never let a decision drift silently on the grounds that "the implementation is already done".
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (constraint 1)

rules.text: Resource format contracts live only in `packages/schema/schemas/` (Schema 单一来源): the TS side (ajv) and the Rust side (jsonschema crate) read the same file, and neither side may keep an inline copy.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) constraint 2; the in-place 「设计依据」 of mod/mod-package.md (schema single source)

rules.text: A schema constrains the resource file format, not Mod logic — the executable interface of a Mod is a Lua script (Lua 唯一可执行接口).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) constraint 2

rules.text: `crates/ygg-core` has a zero-dependency invariant: no internal module, no DOM/platform API, no rendering library; the allowlist is serde / serde_json / thiserror only.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) constraint 3; docs/context/cold-start/principles.md & docs/context/cold-start/topology.md

rules.text: VM dependencies such as mlua may appear only in `crates/ygg-sandbox` (crate 边界).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) constraint 3; the in-place 「设计依据」 of kernel/lua-api.md (crate boundary)

rules.text: Dependency direction is one-way: `ygg-sandbox` → `ygg-core` + `ygg-schema`; `ygg-wasm` → `ygg-sandbox`; `ygg-lint` has no ygg-* kernel dependency; `ygg-schema` and `ygg-core` have no code dependency edge.
rules.basis: docs/context/cold-start/topology.md (inter-module dependency constraints); the Cargo.toml header note of each crate

rules.text: The docs wiki indexed by `docs/README.md` — `docs/context/*` (domain invariants and vocabulary) and `docs/design/*` (three-layer architecture, persistent lane lifecycle, and `harnessActions[]` contracts) — are mandatory references during `plan` and `development` — every subagent brief includes them, and executors must consult them before proposing or editing.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) + docs/{CONTEXT,DESIGN}.md closed loop

rules.text: Runtime projection of `docs/design/mod/mod-package.md` (Mod text hygiene): never reintroduce retired mod/CLI path literals into `data/texts/**` or `data/playbook/**`; only a same-line `[deprecated-ref]` marks a genuine historical reference. Run the specification's grep probe (empty output required) or the semantic test goes red and executors follow a fail-closed path.
rules.basis: docs/design/mod/mod-package.md (runtime projection)

sections.title: 3. Branch management
sections.summary: master accepts merges only; all development happens on feature branches that integrate through the standing `develop` branch (feature → develop → master); every merge is no-FF.
sections.source: Runtime projection of docs/context/acts/release.md and docs/design/host/lanes.md; historical branch rulings remain in git history

rules.text: Never develop directly on master; master accepts merges only.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (branch model)

rules.text: All work (documentation included) happens on a feature branch named `feature/<topic>` or `docs/<topic>`.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (branch model)

rules.text: Every branch merge (feature → develop → master) uses `git merge --no-ff`; fast-forward is forbidden on every hop.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (no-FF invariant)

rules.text: Keep the merge node so an iteration batch (such as `v<date>.<n>`) stays traceable in the history graph and can be rolled back as a whole — that is the purpose of no-FF, not a style preference.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (no-FF invariant)

rules.text: `develop` is the standing integration branch (physical branch name; `origin/develop` exists): every requirement closeout rebases its feature branch onto `develop` and merges it into `develop` with `--no-ff`; `develop` joins `master` only at a round closeout, and no feature branch ever merges into `master` — the only edge into `master` is the round-level `develop` → `master` merge.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Push a feature branch to origin once its verification passes (for collaboration and backup).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (push discipline)

rules.text: Runtime pointer: before any round merge, follow `docs/context/acts/release.md`. That act alone owns the guide/goal trigger, green-evidence precondition and merge cadence; do not treat this chapter as a second merge policy.
rules.basis: r5 batch-3 debt cleanup (merge-state never finalized twice: mt-fde 428ec77 and mxbc 75c2448 left unmerged); user correction 2026-11-13: merging is a normal step — guide = human trigger, goal = agent trigger
